one_line_summary: Table-side digital ordering system for a Kenyan restaurant with live dish availability, party-size-aware ordering, kitchen/bar displays, and a one-directional POS handoff to SambaPOS.
instructions_to_ai: Build exactly the folder and file structure given in 'folder_structure'. Do not invent additional top-level apps or restructure without asking.

Backend is Supabase (Postgres + Realtime + Auth + Edge Functions). Do not introduce a separate custom backend server for guest/staff apps — only the pos-bridge service is a standalone Node process, and it only talks to Supabase and SambaPOS, never to the guest/staff apps directly.

Availability model is 'option 1': is_available lives in the menu_items table and is the single source of truth for guests. Do not derive it from SambaPOS stock unless getMenuAvailability() is explicitly implemented later.

POS integration must go through the POSConnector interface. Implement MockConnector first and make the entire system demoable end-to-end against it. Do not hardcode any SambaPOS-specific GraphQL query until the 'pos_connector_todo' section below is resolved with real values from the venue's SambaPOS instance.
All realtime behavior (menu availability, order status, table state) must use Supabase Realtime subscriptions, not custom polling or a custom WebSocket/SSE server.

Enforce Row Level Security exactly as described in 'rls_policy_summary'. Guests must never be able to read or write another table's session data. pos_sync_log and pos_connector_config must be service-role only.
Currency is KES; timezone default is Africa/Nairobi.
UI must follow 'design_direction' and pull all visual constants from design/design-tokens.json rather than hardcoding values per component.
Ask for clarification rather than guessing if a requirement here is ambiguous — do not silently fill gaps with generic assumptions.

Payments: follow 'payment_security_requirements' exactly. The client must never determine price or payment status. Only the mpesa-callback Edge Function, running with service-role privileges after verifying the callback against a known pending payment, may mark a payment successful. Do not implement any code path where a client request, redirect, or local state alone can mark an order paid.

Do not implement Daraja refund/reversal automation. Refunds are a manual, staff-recorded process in v1 — build the payments.status='refunded' + payment_audit_events record, not an automated money-reversal call.
Never log or display the full raw_callback_payload, full phone numbers, or Daraja credentials anywhere in client-facing code, console output, or committed files.

tech_stack.backend: Supabase (Postgres, Realtime, Auth, Edge Functions, Row Level Security)
tech_stack.pos_bridge: Node.js, runs on-premise on the venue LAN, outbound-only connection to Supabase
tech_stack.styling: Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui components, tokens sourced from design/design-tokens.json

rls_policy_summary.menu_items_categories: public select; insert/update/delete restricted to staff of matching venue_id with role in (chef, bar, admin)
rls_policy_summary.orders_order_items: guests: insert/select only rows matching their JWT's table_session_id claim; staff: select/update for their venue_id
rls_policy_summary.pos_sync_log_pos_connector_config: service-role only, never exposed to anon or authenticated keys
rls_policy_summary.payments: guests: select only (never insert/update) the row matching their own session_id; status transitions happen only inside the service-role mpesa-callback function. staff (admin role only): select for reconciliation; any manual override must go through a function that also writes payment_audit_events, never a direct table update
rls_policy_summary.payment_audit_events: service-role write only; staff (admin) read-only for their venue

methods.getMenuAvailability: () => Promise<Record<string, boolean>> // optional, only if venue's SambaPOS tracks live stock

blocking_questions: Confirm SambaPOS version is V5.x (GraphQL Integration API is V5-only; V4 requires a different approach)
Confirm the venue's Message Server has API access enabled and an Application/access token has been issued for this integration
Run GraphQL schema introspection against the venue's live instance to get exact mutation/field names for ticket creation before writing SambaPosGraphQLConnector
Confirm whether the venue's SambaPOS instance tracks live inventory at all; if not, leave getMenuAvailability() unimplemented and keep availability fully manual
pos_connector_todo.note_to_ai: Do not fabricate SambaPOS GraphQL query/mutation shapes. Leave SambaPosGraphQLConnector as a stub with TODO markers and clear method signatures until these questions are answered with real data from the venue.

payment_security_requirements: Server (Edge Function) computes the payment amount from order_items every time; the client never supplies a price and any client-supplied amount field must be ignored if present.

A payment is only ever marked 'success' by the mpesa-callback Edge Function after it verifies the callback's checkout_request_id matches an existing 'pending' payments row and the amount matches the server-computed order total. No other code path may set status='success'.
mpesa-callback must be idempotent: if a checkout_request_id has already been processed, treat repeat callbacks as a no-op, not a re-credit.

initiate-mpesa-payment must refuse to create a second concurrent pending payment for the same order_id (duplicate-payment protection), and must use idempotency_key to make retried initiation requests safe.

The mpesa-callback URL must use an unguessable path segment (not a predictable route name) since Daraja callbacks are not strongly signed; any callback that doesn't match a known pending payment should be logged as a likely probe, not silently accepted.

Daraja consumer key, secret, and passkey are Supabase Edge Function environment secrets only — never present in guest-pwa, staff-console, or any committed file. .env.example files ship placeholders only.
Rate-limit initiate-mpesa-payment calls per session per time window.
Store phone numbers masked where the full number is not operationally required; never log full phone numbers, Daraja credentials, or raw_callback_payload contents to console/application logs.
Guest-facing payment errors must be generic and actionable ('We couldn't start the payment, please try again') — never a raw Daraja error body or stack trace.

Every payment status transition, including staff manual overrides, writes a payment_audit_events row (who/what/when/previous/new). Refunds in v1 are staff-recorded manual entries, not automated Daraja reversal calls.
If card payments are added later, route them through a hosted checkout (e.g. Pesapal, Flutterwave, DPO) rather than collecting card data directly, to keep PCI-DSS scope off this codebase.

data_flow_summary.guest_order: QR scan -> open-table-session Edge Function issues scoped JWT -> party size set -> menu browsed via Realtime-subscribed query -> cart submitted as orders/order_items (RLS-scoped to session) -> staff console sees it instantly via Realtime -> status updates flow back to guest live -> session close enqueues a pos_sync_log row for the bridge.
data_flow_summary.availability_toggle: Staff toggles menu_items.is_available (or batch_qty_remaining hits 0 via trigger) -> availability_events audit row written -> Realtime pushes change to every subscribed guest session within ~1s -> open carts reconcile client-side.
data_flow_summary.pos_handoff: pos-bridge watches pos_sync_log for status=pending -> calls connector.createTicket() -> writes back pos_ticket_ref + status=success/failed -> staff console can surface failed syncs so nothing silently fails to bill.
data_flow_summary.payment: Guest taps Pay, sends only order_id -> initiate-mpesa-payment computes amount server-side, blocks duplicate concurrent payment, calls Daraja STK push, creates payments row (status=pending) -> guest's PIN prompt happens on their own phone, outside the app -> Safaricom calls mpesa-callback at an unguessable URL -> callback matches checkout_request_id to the pending row, re-verifies amount, is idempotent, updates payments.status and writes payment_audit_events -> only on verified success does the order flip to paid and a pos_sync_log row get enqueued -> guest's pay screen reflects the result live via a Realtime subscription on their own payments row.

design_direction.tone: slick but fast; lightweight assets and short animations since this runs on guest phones over variable venue wifi
design_direction.guest_app: large tap targets, pinned category tabs, item cards with photo + price + one-line description, unavailable items shown greyed-out/strikethrough rather than hidden
design_direction.cart: persistent bottom cart bar with live running total, one clear primary action per screen
design_direction.staff_console: dense, high-contrast, glanceable from arm's length; ticket cards color-coded by age (fresh/aging/urgent)
design_direction.motion: 150-250ms transitions only, purposeful state changes, no decorative animation that delays the next action
design_direction.tokens_source: design/design-tokens.json — all components must read from here, never hardcode colors/spacing/type

non_functional_requirements: Realtime propagation of availability and order status under ~2-3 seconds
Guest app must degrade gracefully on connection loss: cache menu, queue actions, retry on reconnect (not full offline order placement)
No Supabase service-role key ever ships in guest-pwa or staff-console bundles
pos-bridge is the only process with LAN access to SambaPOS and holds the only service-role key with pos_sync_log write scope
Daraja consumer key/secret/passkey exist only as Supabase Edge Function secrets — present in no client bundle and no committed file
Every payment status change is auditable (payment_audit_events) and no payment status can be set by a client-authenticated request
